From: Mr.G.Caldwell, LONDONDERRY


Dear Sir,

I recently bought an art pack
(Artist II) for my +3 computer
(secondhand) but discovered it
was for a +2 computer.

The program loads on tape and
the mouse works perfectly with
it. The problem is that I can't
load, save or print because
these commands in the program
are for the Plus 2 Spectrum.

Could someone tell me what lines
to change in the BASIC programs
to make them compatible with the
Plus 3 on disk.

The programs on Artist II are:
Artist II,Sprite & Font Designer
Page Maker, Screen Compressor.
What BASIC lines must be changed
for each of the above programs.
Please help.
                 George Caldwell

LOAD and SAVE syntax for +3 disc
is the same as for +2 tape.Maybe
your copy has been modified?LIST
and look for commands LOAD and
SAVE. Make sure they are simple
commands such as you'd use on
tape, e.g., LOAD A$ CODE not
LOAD *"M";1;A$ CODE or LOAD D*
etc. I can't see how it could
otherwise fail. Printing is more
complex as ARTIST is notoriously
bugged and I gave up long ago.
Can anyone else offer advice?
                        - Brian

Dear Brian,

Re: Comments in OUTLETTERS 42
    - SAM DRIVE CONNECTIONS.

During the (very short) time I
had a SAM I also suspected the
internal drive was acting
erratically and suspected the
internal connector. By careful
observation through the vent
slots I concluded that if the
drive was inserted into SAM by
pushing on the plastic front
that when it was "fully in" the
connector at the back of the
drive only entered the fixed
socket on the PCB one millimetre
or so.

Comparing a similar type of
connector showed that to be
fully inserted was quite a bit
more that the 1mm or so of this
drive. I found by pushing the
drive into SAM by the actual
drive rather than the case
appeared to fully engage the
connector. BUT (and isn't there
always a BUT!?) this then meant
that the disc was difficult to
eject as the button disappeared
below the level of the face of
the drive front and had to be
pushed with a long finger nail.

I came to the conclusion that
the main PCB should be brought
forward slightly.

Doing tests with a similar (D
type) connector indicated that
the actual contacts in my case
were only engaging about 1/2 mm
or so and with this small amount
of contact I concluded it would
not take much movement due to
knocks or even expansion as
things warmed up to cause prob-
lems.


Here I should add as I only had
Sam for a short while I was not
able to follow up and prove one
way or another. However,it might
be worth investigating with the
problems you are experencing.

128K SPECTRUM VIDEO CONNECTOR:

In addition to the outputs list-
ed, the COMPOSITE VIDEO pin also
carries 6Mhz intercarrier sound.
This is generally not of much
interest or use except to say
that in my case I use a modified
TV where composite video is fed
in after the IF stages and
before the VIDEO/AUDIO stages.
Therefore I get sound on the TV
without the interference on the
screen introduced by the modul-
ator,tv tuner and IF processing.

PLEASE NOTE do NOT delve in TV's
unless you know what you are
doing and the TV is fitted with
as standard or permanently used
with an isolating transformer.

Most mains-only YVs have chassis
metalwork connected direct to
mains AND ARE KILLERS if used
incorrectly or in other than
original manufacturers design.

A second point of interest is in
NEW COMPUTER EXPRESS(9 Feb)there
is a letter stating how to make
BRIGHT work on an Amstrad CTM664
monitor that does not have an
input for BRIGHT:Connect a diode
in series with a 75 ohm resistor
and connect from bright to R (of
RGB). Do the same for G and B (I
understand cathodes go to BRIGHT
pin). I think there was a query
some time back about monitors
that do not support BRIGHT. I've
not tried this myself and do not
know if it would work with other
makes of RGB monitors.

  FIND (Raymond Hoy's problem):

Since OUTLET has got bigger I
have been putting two on a disc
using the DFLIP routine from
FORMAT. This gives some 300k per
side and 160 files per disc.
However, I confirm later OUTLETS
can be converted when the EXIT/
RESET was moved from line 120 to
line 80.

Delete RAND USR 0 and replace
with the LOAD D* "FIND". I tried
the mod with Issue 42 out of
interest and all seemed ok. I am
intending to transfer all the
clipart to a dedicated disc so
that should help to solve the
directory and disc limitations.

I am in the process of posting
off an order for UNIDOS so it
will be interesting to see how
it copes with common file names
in its sub-directories and
increased directory possibil-
ities. Mind you the considerable
reduction in disc prices does
now make the routine less of a
benefit.

It has already been mentioned in
an earlier Outlet but I will
repeat here that I have found it
is better to put the "set issue"
code in the AUTOLOAD routine
rather than in line 9000 as
originally stated. Put in line
50 of AUTOLOAD, just before the
instruction to load CONTENTS.
This is unfortunately nearly at

the end of a long(ish) line. It
could go at the start or even a
separate line but I put it there
so you have the "front cover" to
look at while the issue data is
being erased and updated.

If R. Hoy still has problems and
he would like to send me a disc
with his converted Outlets and
FIND routine etc. that will not
work I will see if I can sort it
out for him (address at head of
this letter).

For those who like to experiment
the time erase and save takes
can be considerably reduced (and
to use a sector just to hold a
single number is a waste). I
have sucessfully used a method

where the current issue is POKED
into the SYS file directory
name. Again this is done in line
50 of AUTOLOAD but is so fast
that it can all go at the start
of the line(or have a line of
its own so it can be added by
merging a pre-written file).

The principle is to lower RAMTOP
to say 50000.Use LOAD @ D,T,S,M
to load the SYS file directory
to 50000 and then POKE in the
code for the Issue number. I.E.,
# 42 would POKE 52 and 50 into
the spaces after SYS name . The
directory is then SAVED back to
disc with SAVE @ D,T,S,M.
Obviously it is best if SYS is
P1 then T=0 and S=1 and the
original name "SYS" will then

change to "SYS 42" or "SYS 41"
depending on the current issue
(Directory if loaded to 50000
then SYS is at 50001, 50002 &
50003 so code 52 is POKED to
50006 & 50 poked to 50007).

FIND is modified to obtain these
codes again using LOAD @ and
PEEK 50006 & 7. These codes are
then converted to a value (42)
and put in the variable I$. This
is a lot more involved but as I
said is considerably faster.

THE LAST WORD: I agree with the
comments about TLW. I suppose I
am biased as I "grew up" with
TLW and it is partly a case of
what one gets used to. However,
I have since acquired TAS 2 but

to be honest I could not get on
with it. I personally, after
TLW, found it far less friendly
and difficult to use. Obviously
with use and if used a lot it
becomes second nature so less of
a problem. However TLW uses
operating and control keys that
relate to the function for the
more commonly-used controls.
Examples: (X=extend mode key
here for ease); X+B=back to
BASIC (main initial menu or exit
to BASIC); x+R=Repeat text;
x+S=Save text;X+L=Load text.
However, as there are a lot of
functions, some use extend
+shift+letter and some do resort
to numbers or non-related
letters but these tend to be
more obscure functions.

The PTC facilities are a marvel
and really user-friendly,both to
set up and incorporate into
text. However, this is not going
to develop into a review. I
could not find anyone selling it
and did not get a reply from my
last known copyright/ publisher
address.I had mine from MGT.
Perhaps someone out there knows
if available, from where and
the cost etc.


Its main virtue is compatibility
(it needs some work to initially
customise) with a wide range of
systems, printers and discs/MD.

   DETECTING THE CURRENT DRIVE
      ON A DISCIPLE AND +D

The drive is selected by switch-
ing on or off a control signal
on one of two lines of the
multiway connector/connecting
cable. There is no feedback from
the drive as such to indicate
which drive is selected but,once
selected, the signal being sent
to the drive is permanent until
reselected. Therefore,the +D and
Disciple at all times dictates
and knows which drive is select-
ed.

Now, in answer to the query from
Brian as to knowing which drive
is selected, I presume it is so


it can be used within a routine,
not simply for the user to know
which drive (which is easy:
simply use the signal to trigger
a circuit driving an LED.).
However,I believe that the
current drive is held in the
DISCIPLE RAM at location 7681 in
the straightforward value 1 for
D1 and 2 for D2. I should think
a PEEK @ this location would
provide the data. The problem is
that there is no PEEK @ in the
BASIC (and a straight PEEK is
into the Spectrum ROM) so a M/C
routine is needed. [I've already
prepared such a routine for the
Disciple and it's in this issue!
- B.C.]. Don't forget, in BASIC,
POKE @ has an offset of 664 on
the Disciple and 8192 on +D.

There was, in fact, a PEEK @
routine published in FORMAT V2
#5 (DEC 88 Page 31). I have
never tried this routine and
have not proved as definite the
disc info location stated above.

In addition to 7681 it is worth
mentioning that it seems 6862
holds 1 for drive 1 and 0 for
drive 2 and that 7642 holds 17
for drive 1 and 16 for drive 2.

I hope this info proves to be of
help and not a red herring. I am
now going to put on my wellies
and fight my way through two
feet of snow drifts to post it
(O.K., I exaggerated a bit - 9
inches really) [Oooo... you
LITT-EL LIAR! - B.C.]

Further to my previous comments
on detecting the drive, A change
of drive can be forced by POKE @
6978,16 or 17. Remember the
Disciple 664 POKE @ offset so
6978 will POKE to location 7642,
POKE @ 0 pokes to location 664.
An example: CAT 2 : LOAD P3 will
load from drive 2. CAT 2 : POKE
@ 6978,17 : LOAD P3. Will load
from drive 1. Remember Disciple
RAM starts at 0 and is 8k.

PLUS D:

+D RAM is above ROM and starts
at 8192 and POKE @ 0 POKEs to
8192 ). In the +D, each of the
locations (in respect of 8k RAM)
6862, 7642 & 7681 hold 1 for
drive 1 and 2 for drive 2.

POKEing does not have immediate
effect as with Disciple but
waits for next drive operation.

Note that POKE @ 7642 is at loc-
ation 7642+8192=15834 on the +D.



ERROR IN #42 OUTLET +D/DISCIPLE
sector copy routine:-

All is O.K. providing D1 is
SOURCE and D2 IS DEST. but if
reversed with Source as D2 there
is a problem. It asks "FORMAT
DRIVE 1?" and if YES it FORMATS
DRIVE 2! Oh hell. Sob, Sob. just
wiped master disc!

ALWAYS write protect discs!!!.

The problem is partly that D1 &
D2 are used as variables but are
also part of disc commands. In
line 250 FORMAT D2 does just
that. It should be FORMAT DD2. A
word of warning: if the routine
is prematurely stoped a CAT will
show a complete directory which
could mislead into thinking all
O.K. It may not be because,
although the directory sectors
have been copied, the data ones
may not have been.

The above is a good case for
sector copy programs to copy the
disc in reverse and do the
directory last. An error would
then be more obvious as
directory would be incomplete or
even missing.  - Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

Thanks, Malcolm. That drive info
is just what I want. I may use
it in my Disciple CATLOADER so
it defaults to the current drive
on loading.

I agree with what you say about
the SAM drives. I have removed
both my drives from their outer
plastic casing and replaced them
in SAM with only the lower half
of the casing. They now fit the
sockets properly. However, it
has not made any difference to
the faults and, as well as look-
ing ugly, the drives chafe on my
wrists! I'll probably put them
back as they were!
                        - Brian

which I originally had with a

From:Mark Battison,SOUTH NORWOOD

Dear Chezron,
             I need help on two
matters - the first is of a
technical nature; the second
concerns my Outlet subscription.

1) Problems with microdrives.
(i.e. The units not the cart-
ridges.) The error message
"Microdrive not present" appears
at virtually every command. Any
solutions? I've changed cart-
ridges (in case one was corrupt,
changed units (as I have 2),
cleaned all edge connectors etc
etc- but still no luck. On very,
very rare occasions, it works -
you can save and load without
any problems, until next time.

The only case where some sort of
response is guaranteed is using
the FORMAT command. In this case
the drive does its first part of
the operation,(flashing borders)
for about 5 secs or so, then
stops with the usual error. I
should have pointed out before
that when you attempt to
load/save etc, the light comes
on and the drive runs for about
1/2 a sec - similar to what
happens if you try to use a
drive without a cartridge in
when the system is working.

Have you any easy solutions, or
is it a repair job? If so, what
is most likely to be at fault;
Microdrive, Interface 1,
computer, some connection???

2) Bearing in mind the above
problems, I've decided the good
old Spectrum is coming to the
end of its life (7 years, almost
exactly). Therefore,replacements
are now being acquired.

To ensure compatability with
most of previous software and
some hardware, I am keeping
within the Spectrum family -
namely the +2A. Together with
the "Amstrad" approved disk
drive - FDI, this should improve
things - both regarding memory
and reliability. The only
question remains - what version
of Outlet! do I now use? I
suspect the +3 version (on disk)
but I thought I'd best check
with you first.

Problem one will still have to
be rectified, because micro-
drives do not work with +2A. (Am
I right in saying this?)

So I will have to transfer any
files I want to use (probably by
tape - if the old Spectrum does
not work the FD-1). Finally, I
hope the +3 version of Outlet!
(or whatever) supports the built
in printer interface on the +2A/
+3 - as the +2A does not seem to
accept the Lprint III interface.

Looking forward to your replies.

              Mark.

To Mark Battison from Brian Gaff

Well, first of all, your
Microdrive problem could be due
to a faulty cable between the
Interface 1 and the drive. There
is a slight possibility that the
Interface 1 itself is failing,
but my money is on the cable,
and/or dirty connections. EEC
seems to sell the cables, by the
way.

The +2A has no provision for
connecting a DD1 directly. If
you read the manual, Amstrad say
you need an add-on called an
SI-1 as an interface. As far as
I am aware, this device has
never been made, and is unlikely
to be, according to Amstrad!

The +2A is a bit of a pig, and
the +D will not work on it with-
out one of my (cough), Fixits,
and then only in 48K mode. If
you go this route, you will need
a 3.5" drive, not a 3" one.

Incidentally, Interface 1 WILL
work on the +2A with my Fixit
but some 128K commands do con-
fuse it at times.

Personally, I would do one of
two things, either sell the +2A
and get a grey +2 from The All
Formats show (Usually around
`70), or alternatively, fit a +2
ROM to your current model, and
buy a special Fixit from me to
fix the port screw-up.

You would then need to get the
+D and drive, which would give
you a Centronics port again. On
the other hand, why not give up
and get a SAM!

                         - B.G.



[BRIAN GAFF'S "FIXIT" is avail-
able from B.G. SERVICES, 64
Roebuck Road, Chessington,Surrey
KT9 1JX for `9.50]

From: Mr. A.A. Blythe, YORK

Dear Ron and Brian,

Re: comments on VDUs/Monitors.
I have found the Phillips CM8833
perfect with Sam. I previously
used it on my Spectrum 128 +2
(Grey Job).

On Sam there is no trace of
ghosting at all. It's fed via
the scart socket - the lead
supplied by MGT. There is a need
to adjust the contrast control
up a bit but brightness can
remain in the central notch.

Audio quality is also quite
good. Quantity is more than I
need in my confined workspace.
But it won't fill a dance hall!!

Using Monitors and TV together
shows the improvement. Also
there is far less of a back-
ground hum on monitors compared
to T.V.

Use of Monitor had one effect on
one particular game I'm fond of,
"Steve Davis Snooker". The brown
ball appears as a slightly
different hue of red in a circle
i.e. not a filled in ball as all
other colours except green -
difficult to show green on green
baize! Yet for some reason the
T.V. output gives a brown filled
in ball.

The same effect was given on the
Spectrum mentioned. Again when
feeding via the Scart socket.

With the Spectrum you can also
feed from Composite Video to the
sockets to the left of the Scart
when looking at the back of the
monitor.

I've seen elsewhere people reco-
mmending made-up leads 5 pin DIN
to twin phono for this purpose
-but there's a drawback. Many of
these leads are pure Audio leads
- too 'lossy' for use at RF(Comp
Video). Combined Audio/Video
leads can be found but one needs
to know what one's looking for.

I made mine up from lightweight
coaxial for the Comp video and a
low loss Audio lead for Audio.
 Coax. 75 or miniature XR88V
 Audio Low noise screened XR18U

The Audio lead is taken to the
audio out on Spectrum +2. Refer
to 128K +2 Manual for pin-outs.
Using this lead I got my brown
ball back on the Snooker game
but overall the Scart gives
better results.

Scart leads:- to enable use of
this socket on +2 I had to
reduce the valves in the scart
plug of resistors in series with
the RGB lines to 10002 from
DD002.  This allowed better
control of the brightness and
contrast from the monitor front
panel.  Steve Davis Snooker runs
in Speccy mode on Sam.

I'm still chuffed to blazes with
your monthly output on Outlet!
               - Tony A. Blythe


Brian Cavers to Tony Blythe


Many thanks for that info, Tony.
I certainly envy you the Philips
monitor. It looks the one to
recommend. Curious though that
there should be such variations
with the Scart "standard".

                       - Brian

From: Donald Akehurst.

Ron,
    Have you changed the print
routine, as my first issue 038
prints out O.K., but the last
two (039 and 040) do not.

My printer-plotter is a Sharp
MZ-1p16 which I made work with
the SPEC +3 in upper case only
(lower case is HEX codes only, I
know why this is) - like the mag
GREAT.
             Regards,

         Donald Akehurst


P.S. I am saving for a Star
printer.

Brian Cavers to Donald Akehurst

Issues 39 and 40 print out with
no problem from my +3. However,
from Issue 39 onwards there are
two code routines included in
the OUTLET loader. These are in
REM statements in the BASIC. The
code at line 1001 stops the auto
boot on error so if you BREAK in
to examine a program it doesn't
reboot when you press ENTER. The
code at line 1002 cures a print
bug that affects some versions
of the +3 which other readers
have reported. It does not seem
possible to overcome both of
them together! The only solution
I can see is for you to do the
following when you wish to print
some OUTLET text...

Enter +3 BASIC from the loader
menu. Enter POKE 23608,0: LOAD
"CONTENTS". Once the CONTENTS
has loaded you should be able to
print out our text. Let me know
the results.

Alternatively, you can start to
boot OUTLET in the normal way(by
RESET and then ENTER) but use
BREAK as soon as the title page
starts to appear, i.e, when the
BASIC loader (saved as "DISK",
of course) has loaded. Now enter
1001 RETURN and 1002 RETURN to
remove the offending code and
RUN 9970 to resave the loader on
the disc. Again, if you try
this, let me know the results.

                        - Brian.

DETECTING THE CURRENT DRIVE ON A DISCIPLE AND +D

The drive is selected by switch- ing on or off a control signal on one of two lines of the multiway connector/connecting cable. There is no feedback from the drive as such to indicate which drive is selected but,once selected, the signal being sent to the drive is permanent until reselected. Therefore,the +D and Disciple at all times dictates and knows which drive is select- ed.

Now, in answer to the query from Brian as to knowing which drive is selected, I presume it is so

it can be used within a routine, not simply for the user to know which drive (which is easy: simply use the signal to trigger a circuit driving an LED.). However,I believe that the current drive is held in the DISCIPLE RAM at location 7681 in the straightforward value 1 for D1 and 2 for D2. I should think a PEEK @ this location would provide the data. The problem is that there is no PEEK @ in the BASIC (and a straight PEEK is into the Spectrum ROM) so a M/C routine is needed. [I've already prepared such a routine for the Disciple and it's in this issue! - B.C.]. Don't forget, in BASIC, POKE @ has an offset of 664 on the Disciple and 8192 on +D.

There was, in fact, a PEEK @ routine published in FORMAT V2 #5 (DEC 88 Page 31). I have never tried this routine and have not proved as definite the disc info location stated above.

In addition to 7681 it is worth mentioning that it seems 6862 holds 1 for drive 1 and 0 for drive 2 and that 7642 holds 17 for drive 1 and 16 for drive 2.

I hope this info proves to be of help and not a red herring. I am now going to put on my wellies and fight my way through two feet of snow drifts to post it (O.K., I exaggerated a bit - 9 inches really) [Oooo... you LITT-EL LIAR! - B.C.]

Further to my previous comments on detecting the drive, A change of drive can be forced by POKE @ 6978,16 or 17. Remember the Disciple 664 POKE @ offset so 6978 will POKE to location 7642, POKE @ 0 pokes to location 664. An example: CAT 2 : LOAD P3 will load from drive 2. CAT 2 : POKE @ 6978,17 : LOAD P3. Will load from drive 1. Remember Disciple RAM starts at 0 and is 8k.

PLUS D:

+D RAM is above ROM and starts at 8192 and POKE @ 0 POKEs to 8192 ). In the +D, each of the locations (in respect of 8k RAM) 6862, 7642 & 7681 hold 1 for drive 1 and 2 for drive 2.

POKEing does not have immediate effect as with Disciple but waits for next drive operation.

Note that POKE @ 7642 is at loc- ation 7642+8192=15834 on the +D.

ERROR IN #42 OUTLET +D/DISCIPLE sector copy routine:-

All is O.K. providing D1 is SOURCE and D2 IS DEST. but if reversed with Source as D2 there is a problem. It asks "FORMAT DRIVE 1?" and if YES it FORMATS DRIVE 2! Oh hell. Sob, Sob. just wiped master disc!

ALWAYS write protect discs!!!.

The problem is partly that D1 & D2 are used as variables but are also part of disc commands. In line 250 FORMAT D2 does just that. It should be FORMAT DD2. A word of warning: if the routine is prematurely stoped a CAT will show a complete directory which could mislead into thinking all O.K. It may not be because, although the directory sectors have been copied, the data ones may not have been.

The above is a good case for sector copy programs to copy the disc in reverse and do the directory last. An error would then be more obvious as directory would be incomplete or even missing.  - Malcolm Perry

FIND модифицируется для считывания этих кодов обратно с помощью `LOAD @` и `PEEK 50006 & 7`. Эти коды затем преобразуются в числовое значение (42) и помещаются в переменную I$. Это несколько сложнее, но, как я уже сказал, работает значительно быстрее.

ОПРЕДЕЛЕНИЕ ТЕКУЩЕГО ДИСКОВОДА НА DISCIPLE И +D

Выбор дисковода осуществляется включением или выключением управляющего сигнала на одной из двух линий многожильного разъёма/соединительного кабеля. Как таковой обратной связи от самого дисковода, показывающей, какой именно дисковод выбран, нет, но после выбора сигнал на дисковод подаётся непрерывно до следующего переключения. Следовательно, +D и Disciple в любой момент времени сами диктуют и точно знают, какой дисковод активен.

Отвечая на вопрос Brian'а о том, как узнать, какой дисковод выбран: я предполагаю, что это требуется внутри подпрограммы, а не просто для визуального контроля пользователя (что проще простого: достаточно использовать сигнал для включения светодиода через схему). Однако я полагаю, что текущий дисковод хранится в ОЗУ DISCIPLE по адресу 7681 в виде простого значения: 1 для D1 и 2 для D2. Думаю, `PEEK @` по этому адресу вернёт нужные данные. Проблема в том, что команды `PEEK @` в BASIC нет (а обычный PEEK читает из ПЗУ Spectrum), поэтому требуется машинная процедура. [Я уже подготовил такую процедуру для Disciple, и она есть в этом номере! — B.C.]. Не забывайте, что в BASIC у команды `POKE @` смещение составляет 664 на Disciple и 8192 на +D.

На самом деле подпрограмма `PEEK @` публиковалась в FORMAT V2 #5 (декабрь 1988, стр. 31). Я сам её ни разу не пробовал и стопроцентно не проверял указанный выше адрес с информацией о диске.

Помимо адреса 7681 стоит упомянуть, что, по всей видимости, ячейка 6862 содержит 1 для дисковода 1 и 0 для дисковода 2, а ячейка 7642 — 17 для дисковода 1 и 16 для дисковода 2.

Надеюсь, эта информация окажется полезной, а не уведёт по ложному следу. Пойду натяну резиновые сапоги и буду пробиваться сквозь двухфутовые сугробы, чтобы отправить это письмо (ладно, приврал немного — на самом деле всего 9 дюймов снега). [О-о-о... ну ты и МА-А-АЛЕНЬКИЙ ВРУНИШКА! — B.C.]

В дополнение к моим предыдущим замечаниям об определении дисковода: переключение привода можно принудительно вызвать командой `POKE @ 6978,16` или `17`. Помните о смещении `POKE @` на 664 у Disciple: соответственно, 6978 запишет в ячейку 7642, а `POKE @ 0` пишет в ячейку 664. Пример: `CAT 2 : LOAD P3` выполнит загрузку со 2-го привода. `CAT 2 : POKE @ 6978,17 : LOAD P3` выполнит загрузку с 1-го привода. Помните, что ОЗУ Disciple начинается с 0 и имеет объём 8 Кб.

PLUS D:

...ОЗУ +D находится выше ПЗУ и начинается с 8192, а POKE @ 0 выполняет POKE в 8192). В +D каждая из ячеек (относительно 8K ОЗУ) 6862, 7642 и 7681 содержит 1 для дисковода 1 и 2 для дисковода 2.

POKE не действует мгновенно, как на Disciple, а ожидает следующей операции с дисководом.

Обратите внимание, что POKE @ 7642 на +D находится по адресу 7642+8192=15834.

Код в строке 1002 исправляет ошибку печати, встречающуюся на некоторых версиях +3, о чем сообщали другие читатели. Похоже, совместить их без конфликтов невозможно! Единственное решение, которое я вижу — делать следующее, если вы хотите распечатать текст из OUTLET:

Выйдите в +3 BASIC из меню загрузчика. Введите:

```text
POKE 23608,0: LOAD "CONTENTS"
```

Как только CONTENTS загрузится, вы сможете напечатать наш текст. Дайте знать о результатах.

В качестве альтернативы вы можете начать загрузку OUTLET обычным способом (через RESET, а затем ENTER), но нажать BREAK, как только начнет появляться титульная страница, то есть когда загрузится BASIC-загрузчик (сохраненный, конечно же, как "DISK"). Теперь введите 1001 RETURN и 1002 RETURN, чтобы удалить проблемный код, и RUN 9970, чтобы перезаписать загрузчик на диск. Опять же, если вы попробуете это сделать, дайте мне знать о результатах.
